conventions: tml-renderers receives OpenAI Chat messages through chat.OpenAIMessage.from_openai_chat_dicts(messages, tools=tools) and renders with renderers.Inkling2().render_for_completion_with_effort(messages, effort).
The tool declaration that the OpenAI bridge emits first is moved after the leading system messages, the order SGLang and tinker-cookbook use.

Every prompt carries the effort message; an absent effort is 0.9. Named efforts map through the checkpoint chat template's table; enable_thinking=false, Responses reasoning.effort=none and Messages thinking.type=disabled select effort 0. tml-renderers has no named efforts, thinking switch or tool_choice.
Efforts above 0.99 are rejected, as SGLang's Inkling serving and the checkpoint template reject them; tml-renderers itself accepts efforts up to 1.
Flare lowers developer instructions into one leading system message labeled 'System instructions:' and 'Developer instructions:' when any developer message is present.

tool_choice=none removes the tool declaration; a named tool_choice declares only that tool; tool_choice=required appends Flare's required-tool instruction to the first system message, inserting one when absent.
A tool result's own name names its frames; tml-renderers names an unnamed result after the most recent preceding call with its tool_call_id.
Flare orders a batch of tool results by the order of their calls.
A failed tool result renders the text part 'Tool execution failed:' before its content parts.
A JSON-schema response format appends Flare's schema instruction to the first system message.
A tool declared without parameters receives Flare's default schema {"type":"object","properties":{}}.
Continuing the final assistant message renders it without its end-of-turn token and leaves its last frame open by removing that frame's <|end_message|>.
Each image renders as one <|content_image|> frame; input_ids hold one placeholder token per image.
